send_policy.name: deadline-20s-retry-60s-skip
send_policy.deadline_scope: from the journaled start of the try, including the sent-line fsync, DNS, connect, TLS, request write, response headers and the whole body. A timer thread shuts the socket down when monotonic time reaches the budget, or sooner if civil time jumps ahead. Keep-alive bytes do not extend it, and a backward civil-time step cannot extend it either.
send_policy.retried: timeouts, dropped or incomplete reads, TLS and DNS errors, HTTP 429 and 5xx

observed_mean: For each family, use the archived flight with the higher mean off-peak all-miss cost per arm-turn, taking that flight's prompt, output, and steps together. Apply it to this draw's user turns and four arms. The long-context spike and the 21-step memory turn are allowance tails, not part of this mean.
higher_step: For each family, the archived flight with the higher mean steps per arm-turn, with that flight's own prompt and output. Four arms on the full catalogue's user turns.
time_rule: Serial. Seconds per send are the profile pace plus hang rate times the 20 s first deadline; the retry that follows a hang is already a send. No backoff after a deadline (FULL_FLY_POLICY), 2 s after an HTTP status. A send inside a peak window costs double. Hung first tries are priced at their case's mean cost per send, as if billed.
ceiling_floor: The CLI refuses --full with a ceiling under this. It is the costliest observed-mean or higher-step profile with its peak premium and its hung first tries priced as billed, rounded up to the cent. It is not a recommendation; Jacky names the ceiling.
allowance_with_monday_peak: The planning upper at 1.9 s, no hangs, from Friday 18:00 HKT: it finishes Monday evening and its Monday 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00 sends cost double.
ten_hours_verdict: Not feasible on the serial runner. The mean path alone is about 37 hours of successful requests at 1.9 s; ten hours would need about four requests in flight all the time. The 20 s / 60 s policy cuts hang waste, not work.
superseded_not_to_fly: any full 12,952-slot command without --full (no 20 s / 60 s deadlines, no skip-and-record, no resume)

render_identity.formula: sha256 of one line per render: case_id, state, arm, tools_sha256, separated by NUL and ended by a newline. tools_sha256 is sha256(json.dumps(tools, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)), the attempts.jsonl formula. state is initial, then held_out:<turn> after each held-out batch in the order the runner appends them. Arms are U, S, X, SX.

frozen_plan: full/cost.json is the gate file the CLI reads. It was priced at 6d4081e3 with editors s-rules-2026-11-26 and x-rules-2026-11-26. This file is the same report recomputed with the editors above. The ceiling floor, the observed-mean path and the higher-step path match that gate file. The CLI records the gate file's planning_upper_usd in the run identity. It does not read this file.
